extracted.intended_audience: veterans and general newspaper readers interested in postwar benefits, government policy and labor news
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper page combining a Q&A summary of amended GI Bill and veteran benefits (entitlements, subsistence, loans, rehabilitation) with related postwar policy and labor news (OPA/CPA actions, WSA authority, GM fact-finding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Course entitlement based on length of service
rubrics_metrics.description: A veteran is entitled to one course costing $500 for each year of service; if he is eligible for several courses all may be taken in one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost is figured on the basis of length of war service; entitlement expressed as $500 per year of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: No subsistence for correspondence courses
rubrics_metrics.description: A veteran may take a correspondence course and its cost will be paid, but no subsistence will be paid while taking a correspondence course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total amount payable for a correspondence course is $500; correspondence course cost is paid but subsistence payments are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased subsistence allowances for schooling
rubrics_metrics.description: The amended bill increases subsistence allowances: from $50 a month for single men to $65; from $75 for married men to $90.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the new monthly rates distinguishing single and married veterans under the amended bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocational training completion timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Disabled veterans must complete vocational training within nine years after the war's end (previously six years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended bill extends the period of eligibility for vocational training to nine years after war's end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsistence during vocational rehabilitation for disabled veterans
rubrics_metrics.description: Disabled veterans will receive a minimum of $105 per month if without dependents; $115 with a dependent plus $10 for the first child, $7 for each additional child and $15 for a dependent parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the veteran receives a lesser pension he will receive these amounts while in training; in no event will his pension be reduced when he enters training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-estate loan guarantee limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will guarantee a real estate loan for a veteran up to $4,000 (compared with $2,000 under the original bill).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government guarantees up to 50 percent of the total loan against a veteran's property, but not to exceed $4,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government guarantee limit for business loans
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will guarantee business loans, but the limit of the Government guarantee remains at $2,000 or 50 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business loan guarantees remain at prior limits despite changes to real-estate loan guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real estate appraisal standard for VA loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Phraseology is changed from 'reasonable normal value' to 'reasonable value' in the amended bill; the appraisal must be acceptable to the lender, the veteran and a Veterans Administration-designated appraiser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the standard/parties whose acceptance is required for appraisal in loan underwriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deduction of GI Bill benefits from future bonus
rubrics_metrics.description: The portion of the law providing that any financial benefits received under the act would be deducted from a future bonus is repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GI Bill financial benefits will not be offset against any future bonus under the repealed provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: VA provision for prosthetic appliance and transport payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Veterans Administration may obtain the limb (prosthetic appliance) and pay to and from a center where the appliance is fitted and the veteran is trained in the use of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA may cover acquisition and transport related to fitting and training for prosthetic appliances.

rubrics_metrics.name: WSA authority to operate water carrier service (extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Shipping Administration was authorized to operate water carrier service from Dec. 31, 1945 to June 30, 1946 through agents holding certificates previously issued by the commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step taken to permit resumption of water service pending disposition of vessels requisitioned for war service.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPA/CPA action on misused textile priority ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPA ordered cancellation of outstanding rated textile orders in excess of quarterly authorizations and directed mills to place no rated orders for textiles for the first three months of next year unless specifically authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension intended to punish manufacturers who 'kited' ratings (obtained inflated priority ratings); manufacturers violating rating regulations will be hard pressed to get textiles and will face investigations and possible referral to the Department of Justice for willful violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper and paperboard allocation and conservation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper controls (allocation) being revoked with inventory limits retained; paper-conservation order M-241 would be canceled; paper mills required to set aside 10 percent of production for government and other essential needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialty papers not sold at retail; inventory and allocation adjustments timed with revocation of some controls but retention of minimum inventory restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA enforcement and hearings for priority misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers suspended for misuse of priorities will face investigation and a hearing; willful violations will be referred to the Department of Justice for criminal action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA compliance division investigations revealed 'kiting' of ratings by 50 to 400 percent; suspension remains pending completion of investigation and hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer's Council scarce-materials list limiting construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Material shortages (millwork, enameled plumbing fixtures, heating equipment, possibly cast iron soil pipe) would limit construction to not more than 452,000 privately built dwellings in 1946 unless the Government encouraged production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortages attributed to pricing, manpower problems and raw material shortages slowing production.

rubrics_metrics.name: New withholding schedule effective Jan 1, 1946
rubrics_metrics.description: A revised withholding schedule for payroll withholdings becomes effective January 1, 1946, with columns representing single persons, married couples without children, married couples with one child, two children, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reductions in withholdings will reduce tax burdens for many individuals; examples and table given illustrating impact by earnings and family size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of individual surtax exemptions to normal tax
rubrics_metrics.description: The new law applies individual surtax exemptions (for taxpayer and $500 per dependent) to the normal tax, resulting in no income tax until net earnings exceed specified thresholds (e.g., $1,000 for single person).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how exemptions change tax start thresholds and gives numeric examples for various family situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of excess-profits tax and corporate surtax reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 85.5 percent excess-profits tax on corporations is repealed; declared value excess-profits levies repealed and combined normal surtaxes reduced by two to four percent depending on earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the first postwar tax reduction law intended to reduce corporate tax burdens and stimulate reconversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-finding board criteria for assessing 'ability to pay' (GM case)
rubrics_metrics.description: In assessing 'ability to pay' the board would consider costs, prices, prospective volume of business, investment factors, expenses and the entire forward operating program of the business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Motors objects that assessing 'ability to pay' would require appraising factors that are effectively managerial responsibilities and thus would assume vital management functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of wage-increase recommendation based on production
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact-finding board may recommend a wage increase for either the first year of the union's new contract or for the first postwar production year, depending on whether production reaches capacity and strike effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board's decision contingent on capacity production and whether pandemic/strike conditions make 1946 a 'normal' production year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-finders' process and data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact-finding board was given twenty days to prepare its report and will obtain government data (e.g., from Commerce Department, Securities and Exchange Commission) and hear public testimony, including union and company evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board to consider presented economic facts, profit figures, wage data and other evidence in making recommendations on labor disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union methodology for estimating corporate profits in bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Union estimated General Motors' 1946 profits by assuming 1942 selling prices, materials costing 15 percent more than 1941, and inclusion of a 30 percent wage increase, producing a $561,000,000 profit estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Union presented mass of charts and figures; the fact-finding board questioned whether strike-related disruptions might alter these estimates.
